hero.headline: Body found in Martin County mangroves believed to be missing Port St. Lucie man Michael Debevec
hero.teaser: A body discovered deep within the mangroves near the House of Refuge in Martin County is believed to be that of Michael Anthony Debevec, a Port St. Lucie man reported missing in Au
hero.body:
A body discovered deep within the mangroves near the House of Refuge in Martin County is believed to be that of Michael Anthony Debevec, a Port St. Lucie man reported missing in August. Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek announced Tuesday that investigators recovered the body after an extensive search, but decomposition prevented officials from confirming the cause of death.

 The deceased person was wearing clothing matching what Debevec was believed to have been wearing. Debevec's family was notified that a body was found, though official identification was still pending.

 The search began Saturday after a Good Samaritan found a wallet belonging to Debevec and went to his home to return it, prompting his family to file a missing person report. Investigators found Debevec's vehicle Saturday afternoon at Chastain Beach, a little more than two miles from where the body was discovered. Detectives and ground and aerial units launched an extensive search following the discovery of the wallet and vehicle.

 Investigators determined that Debevec traveled from the Port St. Lucie area to Martin County at about 3 a.m. on the 27th and parked at Chastain Beach. Phone records showed that his phone was in use Friday morning and moving back and forth between Chastain Beach and the House of Refuge. On Tuesday morning, investigators found a backpack belonging to Debevec hanging high in a tree with his computer inside.

 A deeper search into the mangroves led investigators to the body. Budensiek said investigators had not officially confirmed whether the body was Debevec's. "So we do believe we found Mr. Unfortunately, there's a lot of decomposition that's taken place so it's really impossible to determine cause of death.

 What are we dealing with here? I don't know?" Budensiek said during a news conference Tuesday.

cards.headline: Vero Beach man accused of AI deepfake scheme held on $1 million bond
cards.teaser: Peter Solomon Ruma, 37, is being held in the Indian River County Jail on $1 million bond after his Wednesday arrest on charges of creating and distributing AI-generated sexually explicit images of women without consent.
cards.body:
A Vero Beach man arrested Wednesday on charges for creating and distributing AI-generated sexually explicit images of women without consent is now being held in the Indian River County Jail on $1 million bond. Peter Solomon Ruma, 37, faces eight specific charges including creating and promoting altered sexual depictions after Vero Beach police executed search warrants and recovered forensic evidence. The $1 million bond reflects the severity of the charges against him.

 Investigators say Ruma has been engaging in this activity for several years. Police said he downloaded photographs of women from social media platforms and used artificial intelligence technology to manipulate the images by digitally removing clothing and creating sexual scenarios. The manipulated images were then distributed without the consent of the individuals depicted.

 Ruma worked as a driver for Lyft and Uber Eats, according to police. Complaints involving similar behavior date back several years, and authorities are warning that additional victims may exist beyond those identified in the initial charges.

 Police are encouraging anyone who believes they may have been victimized to come forward. The investigation remains active as officials work to identify the full scope of the alleged scheme.

cards.headline: Palm City woman charged in Border Collie hoarding case released from jail on $500 bond
cards.teaser: Paige O'Donnell, 62, posted a $500 surety bond and was released from jail Monday after pleading not guilty to 72 charges stemming from the rescue of 36 Border Collies from her Palm City home last month.
cards.body:
Paige O'Donnell, 62, posted a $500 surety bond and was released from jail on Monday after pleading not guilty to 72 charges stemming from the rescue of 36 Border Collies from her Palm City home last month, according to Martin County court documents. O'Donnell faces 36 third-degree felony counts involving alleged animal cruelty and 36 misdemeanor counts alleging animals were kept without sufficient exercise and air.

The charges stem from last month when the 36 Border Collies were recovered from O'Donnell's Palm City home in deplorable conditions. O'Donnell, a former dog breeder, was at the center of the investigation after authorities found the dogs at her residence.

O'Donnell hired an attorney who filed a waiver of appearance for her at pre-trial hearings and entered a plea of not guilty to the charges. She has legally surrendered the dogs to the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast for adoption.

Adoption applications for the Border Collies opened on Tuesday. No future court dates are currently listed in the case, according to court records.

cards.headline: Former DeSantis spokesperson's PR firm awarded more than $700K in state contracts, drawing watchdog scrutiny
cards.teaser: A public relations firm owned by a former spokesperson for Governor Ron DeSantis has been awarded more than $700,000 in state government contracts across multiple Florida agencies
cards.body:
A public relations firm owned by a former spokesperson for Governor Ron DeSantis has been awarded more than $700,000 in state government contracts across multiple Florida agencies over the past three years, raising questions from a nonpartisan watchdog group about whether political loyalty influenced the awards. State records show that TMF Communications, owned by Taryn Fenske, has secured five- and six-figure contracts for PR consulting work from several agencies since 2023, including the Department of Health, the Department of Children and Families, the Agency for Persons with Disabilities, New College, and the Justice Administration Commission. Fenske, a former GOP communications director who worked for DeSantis' executive communications team and later his presidential super PAC, launched the private firm after DeSantis' presidential run ended.

 The contracts include nearly $40,000 from the Department of Health earlier this year, $113,000 from DCF in 2025 to support digital media vendors, $75,000 from the Agency for Persons with Disabilities in 2025 for rebranding work, another $52,000 allocation in 2026, more than $400,000 from New College since 2023 for PR consulting, and nearly $27,000 from the Justice Administration Commission in 2023 to assist with public relations after DeSantis suspended Orange County State Attorney Monique Worrell. Fenske built her political career in Tallahassee working for former Governor Rick Scott, the Republican National Committee, and Education Commissioner Richard Corcoran before joining the DeSantis administration.

 Ben Wilcox, who leads Integrity Florida, a nonpartisan government watchdog group, criticized the arrangement after reviewing the contract records. "I think to the average citizen, the average taxpayer, that that's an exorbitant amount of money," Wilcox said. "I think it looks bad to the public. I think it looks like this communications consultant is being rewarded for her service to the DeSantis administration and to Governor DeSantis personally."

 Fenske declined to speak on camera but called the premise that her loyalty to the DeSantis administration contributed to her state work "insulting and dismissive" of her professional qualifications in an email. She said her company's work was "earned on its merits." Alex Lanfranconi, DeSantis' current communications director, called TMF's state business "awesome" and described Fenske as "one of the best communications professionals in the state." DCF defended its contract with Fenske and noted that TMF appears on a list of state-approved PR vendors as neither the least nor the most expensive option.

hero.headline: Palm City woman charged in Border Collie hoarding case released from jail on $500 bond
hero.teaser: Paige O'Donnell, 62, posted a $500 surety bond and was released from jail Monday after pleading not guilty to 72 charges stemming from the rescue of 36 Border Collies from her Palm City home last month.
hero.body:
Paige O'Donnell, 62, posted a $500 surety bond and was released from jail on Monday after pleading not guilty to 72 charges stemming from the rescue of 36 Border Collies from her Palm City home last month, according to Martin County court documents. O'Donnell faces 36 third-degree felony counts involving alleged animal cruelty and 36 misdemeanor counts alleging animals were kept without sufficient exercise and air.

The charges stem from last month when the 36 Border Collies were recovered from O'Donnell's Palm City home in deplorable conditions. O'Donnell, a former dog breeder, was at the center of the investigation after authorities found the dogs at her residence.

O'Donnell hired an attorney who filed a waiver of appearance for her at pre-trial hearings and entered a plea of not guilty to the charges. She has legally surrendered the dogs to the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast for adoption.

Adoption applications for the Border Collies opened on Tuesday. No future court dates are currently listed in the case, according to court records.

hero.headline: Body found in Martin County mangroves believed to be missing Port St. Lucie man Michael Debevec
hero.teaser: A body discovered deep within the mangroves near the House of Refuge in Martin County is believed to be that of Michael Anthony Debevec, a Port St. Lucie man reported missing in Au
hero.body:
A body discovered deep within the mangroves near the House of Refuge in Martin County is believed to be that of Michael Anthony Debevec, a Port St. Lucie man reported missing in August. Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek announced Tuesday that investigators recovered the body after an extensive search, but decomposition prevented officials from confirming the cause of death.

 The deceased person was wearing clothing matching what Debevec was believed to have been wearing. Debevec's family was notified that a body was found, though official identification was still pending.

 The search began Saturday after a Good Samaritan found a wallet belonging to Debevec and went to his home to return it, prompting his family to file a missing person report. Investigators found Debevec's vehicle Saturday afternoon at Chastain Beach, a little more than two miles from where the body was discovered. Detectives and ground and aerial units launched an extensive search following the discovery of the wallet and vehicle.

 Investigators determined that Debevec traveled from the Port St. Lucie area to Martin County at about 3 a.m. on the 27th and parked at Chastain Beach. Phone records showed that his phone was in use Friday morning and moving back and forth between Chastain Beach and the House of Refuge. On Tuesday morning, investigators found a backpack belonging to Debevec hanging high in a tree with his computer inside.

 A deeper search into the mangroves led investigators to the body. Budensiek said investigators had not officially confirmed whether the body was Debevec's. "So we do believe we found Mr. Unfortunately, there's a lot of decomposition that's taken place so it's really impossible to determine cause of death.

 What are we dealing with here? I don't know?" Budensiek said during a news conference Tuesday.

hero.headline: Vero Beach man accused of AI deepfake scheme held on $1 million bond
hero.teaser: Peter Solomon Ruma, 37, is being held in the Indian River County Jail on $1 million bond after his Wednesday arrest on charges of creating and distributing AI-generated sexually explicit images of women without consent.
hero.body:
A Vero Beach man arrested Wednesday on charges for creating and distributing AI-generated sexually explicit images of women without consent is now being held in the Indian River County Jail on $1 million bond. Peter Solomon Ruma, 37, faces eight specific charges including creating and promoting altered sexual depictions after Vero Beach police executed search warrants and recovered forensic evidence. The $1 million bond reflects the severity of the charges against him.

 Investigators say Ruma has been engaging in this activity for several years. Police said he downloaded photographs of women from social media platforms and used artificial intelligence technology to manipulate the images by digitally removing clothing and creating sexual scenarios. The manipulated images were then distributed without the consent of the individuals depicted.

 Ruma worked as a driver for Lyft and Uber Eats, according to police. Complaints involving similar behavior date back several years, and authorities are warning that additional victims may exist beyond those identified in the initial charges.

 Police are encouraging anyone who believes they may have been victimized to come forward. The investigation remains active as officials work to identify the full scope of the alleged scheme.
